correctness.rationale: On inputs n>=2 with Omega(n)<=2, tau(n) can only be 2 (prime), 3 (prime square), or 4 (squarefree product of two distinct primes). In a collision F(m)=F(n) with m<n we require n-m=tau(m)-tau(n)>0. Thus possible pairs of divisor counts are exactly (3,2), (4,2), (4,3). The first forces (m,n)=(4,5) because p²+1 prime only for p=2; the second gives exactly m=qr with distinct odd primes q<r and n=qr+2 prime, and the converse is immediate; the third would force qr=p²−1 divisible by 8 for odd p, impossible for squarefree qr of v2<=1 (p=2 also impossible). Distinct possible pairs share no third value in the restricted domain, so max fiber cardinality is 2. Independent sieve over 2<=n<=100000 computed all F-fibers on Omega<=2, finding 2,961 nontrivial fibers and no counterexample; symbolic case exhaustion, not finite scan, proves infinite assertion.
